Subject: Capacity escrow trigger: AvalonAI late-stage commit

Marcus —

Quick heads-up: Avalon (Emily) called this morning; they verbally committed to go-live with a controlled production footprint targeted for the first week of Sept. High level ask: a provisional capacity hold (soft escrow) to cover sustained inference of roughly 1.4B tokens/month initially — our estimate maps to ~16 A100-equivalent GPUs sustained for baseline traffic (burst to 24 for scheduled retraining windows).

Can you do a near-term availability check and tell me:
- whether we can tag a soft hold for that footprint in us-west (preferred) and for what date range
- preemption risk (any scheduled maintenance or capacity contention in early Sept)
- recommended conservative allocation (if ops prefers smaller initial buffer + autoscale vs full 16)
- whether we can reserve a dedicated slice to avoid noisy-neighbor risk or whether a dedicated pool is required

I'm attaching the MOU draft and our allocation projection so you have the expected token curve and ramp. If we can get a soft-engineering sign-off today, I'll circulate the brief to the Avalon procurement lead and attach the MOU for signature. Lauren, Ben — looping you for customer contact and billing touchpoints.

Deal reference: DEAL-2026-4821. Region: us. Target prod start: 2026-09-04.

Attachments: avalonai_mou_v0.2.pdf, gpu-allocation-projection.xlsx

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
---

Karthik —

Thanks for the heads-up and for the attachments. Quick snapshot from infra:
- us-west dedicated pool (primary): nominal capacity available this week: ~48 A100-equivalent GPUs free across 12 pods.
- scheduled infra maintenance window: 2026-09-10 (rolling updates affecting ~8 GPUs for a 6-hour window) — can be shifted if this deal is mission-critical but will need ops approval.
- contention risk: moderate in late Sept (Q4 onboarding wave) — we should avoid full long-term allocation without a signed commitment.

Recommendation: place a soft hold for 12 GPUs in us-west starting 2026-09-04 for a 90-day provisional window; enable autoscale to burst to 20 GPUs if usage requires. This balances availability vs inventory exposure. If Avalon signs a 12-month reserved capacity contract we can lock the full 16+ slice and schedule maintenance around their SLA.

Actionables I can do from ops side:
1) open an internal hold ticket and tag 12 GPUs as SOFT-HOLD (non-billing) — will surface as CAP-HOLD-2026-9981 (preliminary).
2) add a note to the maintenance calendar to avoid 9/4–9/11 for that slice.
3) prepare a dedicated pod layout if we need noisy-neighbor isolation (adds ~6–8 hour setup and 1 additional node overhead).

Questions:
- can Avalon accept an initial 12-GPU buffer with defined burst to 20? (we'll require MOU amendment to specify burst rules)
- confirm final start date and whether they want dedicated pod isolation.

If you want, I can stand up the provisional hold now and we can escalate to a full reserved allocation once MOU signed.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Lead, Capacity Planning | Redwood Inference
